result.title: Distillation, Self-Training, and the Fragility of Learned Chemical Reasoning
result.summary: Automating synthesis planning for small-molecule drug design requires chemical reasoners that are accurate as well as open to inspection and adaptation, yet frontier language models remain unreliable at predicting reaction outcomes and difficult to deploy, while small open-weight models lack the necessary domain reasoning. We show that frontier supervision can serve as a one-time bootstrap for open models on forward reaction prediction. Our models, Resonance, distill an open-weight teacher's reasoning traces and then learn from their own verified outputs, turning a small base model with near-zero accuracy into a capable reaction predictor, while a stronger student surpasses its teacher through distillation alone. Accuracy, however, does not bring robust reasoning: the small student inherits its teacher's single-pass style, self-training mainly sharpens answers it could already reach, and it readily abandons correct answers under pushback, suggesting that chemical reasoning models should be evaluated on the robustness of their reasoning as well as on the accuracy of their answers.

AI.brief_summary: 论文训练开放权重小模型做正向反应预测（Resonance）：先用前沿模型的推理轨迹蒸馏，再用自己验证过的输出做自训练，发现准确率可大幅提升甚至超过教师，但推理并不鲁棒，自训练主要只是强化模型本已能得到的答案，模型在受到质疑时容易放弃正确答案。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「蒸馏轨迹＋自训练是否真的带来推理能力、还是只强化已有答案」的诊断，可能为 LVR 中轨迹监督与「latent 内容是否真正被用于答案」的贡献分配与旁路问题提供可核查的线索。
